examples.en: If you memorize the times tables, division gets easy too.
I solved ten division problems.
My child is good at addition but finds division hard.
In division, there is sometimes a remainder.
Doing division on a calculator is fast.
Teacher, what's the answer to this division problem?

explain: 덧셈, 뺄셈, 곱셈, 나눗셈이 사칙연산 짝이에요. 식을 읽을 때는 '육 나누기 이는 삼'처럼 '나누기'를 써요. '나눗셈'은 사이시옷이 있어서 '나누셈'이 아니라 '나눗셈'으로 써요.
explain_en: It belongs with 덧셈, 뺄셈 and 곱셈 as the four arithmetic operations. When you read an equation aloud, you say '육 나누기 이는 삼' with '나누기'. Spell it with the ㅅ: 나눗셈, not 나누셈.

examples.en: The cat jumped lightly up onto the wall.
The children are so excited that they bounce up and down.

examples.ko: 돌고래가 물 위로 높이 뛰어오르는 모습을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a dolphin leaping high out of the water.

examples.ko: 저 선수는 정말 높이 뛰어오를 수 있어요.
examples.en: That athlete can jump really high.

examples.ko: 개구리가 갑자기 내 발 위로 뛰어올라서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A frog suddenly jumped onto my foot and startled me.
I was running up the stairs and fell.

explain: '뛰다'와 '오르다'가 합쳐진 말이라서 위로 힘껏 뛰는 동작이나 달려서 위로 올라가는 동작에 써요. 반대말은 '뛰어내리다'예요. '오르다'가 르 불규칙이라서 '뛰어올라요, 뛰어올랐어요'가 돼요.
explain_en: Combining '뛰다' and '오르다', it describes jumping up energetically or running upward. The opposite is '뛰어내리다'. Because '오르다' is a 르-irregular verb, it becomes '뛰어올라요' and '뛰어올랐어요'.

examples.en: On the weekend I went roller skating in the park.
It was my first time roller skating, so I kept falling.
I bought the protective gear needed for roller skating.
My younger sibling is really good at roller skating.

examples.ko: 롤러스케이트 탈 때는 보호대를 꼭 하세요.
examples.en: Be sure to wear protective gear when roller skating.
As a kid I often went to the roller skating rink.

explain: 스케이트를 탈 때처럼 '롤러스케이트를 타다'라고 하고 '하다'는 쓰지 않아요. 바퀴가 한 줄로 달린 '인라인스케이트'도 있어요. 넘어질 수 있어서 손목, 무릎 보호대를 같이 말하곤 해요.
explain_en: Like other skating, you say '롤러스케이트를 타다', not '하다'. There is also '인라인스케이트', with the wheels in one line. Because you can fall, people often mention wrist and knee guards along with it.

examples.en: I'm learning boxing for exercise.
Boxing is a sport that needs a lot of stamina.
On the weekend I watched a boxing match on TV.

examples.ko: 집 근처에 새로 생긴 복싱장에 등록했어요.
examples.en: I signed up at the newly opened boxing gym near my home.
My father was a boxer when he was young.
I put on boxing gloves and hit the punching bag.

explain: 복싱과 권투는 같은 운동이에요. 운동하는 곳은 '복싱장'이나 '체육관', 선수는 '복서' 또는 '권투 선수'라고 해요.
explain_en: 복싱 and 권투 are the same sport. You train at a 복싱장 or 체육관, and the athlete is a 복서 or 권투 선수.

examples.ko: 이 니트는 세탁기 말고 손빨래해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to hand-wash this knit, not use the washing machine.
Hand-washing is hard work, but it damages clothes less.
I just quickly hand-washed a few pairs of socks.
Winter blankets are too heavy to wash by hand.
Hand-wash expensive blouses in cold water.
I heard people used to do all the laundry by hand.

explain: '손빨래를 하다'와 '손빨래하다' 둘 다 자연스러워요. 세탁기로 빠는 것과 달리 손으로 직접 빠는 것이라서, 옷 라벨에 '손세탁'이라고 쓰여 있을 때가 있어요. 맡겨서 빠는 건 '세탁소에 맡기다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Both '손빨래를 하다' and '손빨래하다' sound natural. It contrasts with washing by machine, and clothing labels sometimes say '손세탁' (hand wash). Sending clothes out is '세탁소에 맡기다' (leave at the laundry).

examples.en: I fell and hurt my left arm.
I'm wearing a watch on my left arm.
My left arm hurt, so I carried the bag on the right.
The doctor gave me a shot in the left arm.

examples.ko: 저는 왼팔보다 오른팔이 더 힘이 세요.
examples.en: My right arm is stronger than my left arm.

examples.ko: 왼팔로 아이를 안고 오른손으로 문을 열었어요.
examples.en: I held the child with my left arm and opened the door with my right hand.

explain: '왼'은 왼팔, 왼손, 왼발, 왼쪽처럼 몸의 왼쪽을 나타내요. 반대말 '오른팔'은 '사장님의 오른팔'처럼 가장 믿는 부하를 뜻하기도 하지만, 왼팔에는 그런 뜻이 없어요.
explain_en: 왼 marks the left side, as in 왼팔, 왼손, 왼발 and 왼쪽. The opposite 오른팔 can also mean a most trusted right-hand person (사장님의 오른팔), but 왼팔 has no such meaning.

examples.en: I'm going to a language school to learn Indonesian.
Indonesian uses the alphabet, so it's easy to read.

examples.ko: 친구가 인도네시아어로 인사하는 법을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend taught me how to greet in Indonesian.
I have a friend who works as an Indonesian interpreter.
For me, Korean is harder than Indonesian.

examples.ko: 이 책은 한국어와 인도네시아어로 쓰여 있어요.
examples.en: This book is written in Korean and Indonesian.

explain: 나라 이름 뒤에 '-어'를 붙이면 그 나라 언어 이름이 돼요. 영어, 일본어처럼요. 방법을 나타내는 '로'를 붙여 '인도네시아어로 말하다'처럼 써요. '인도네시아 말'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: Adding '-어' after a country name gives the name of its language, as in 영어 and 일본어. Add '로' to show the means, as in '인도네시아어로 말하다' (speak in Indonesian). You can also say '인도네시아 말'.

examples.ko: 이 폰은 터치가 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: The touch on this phone doesn't work well.

examples.ko: 터치 한 번으로 주문할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can order with a single touch.
Lightly touch the phone screen with your finger.
The painting was finished with the artist's last touch.

examples.ko: 장갑을 끼고 터치스크린을 누르면 반응이 없어요.
examples.en: If you press a touchscreen with gloves on, it doesn't respond.

examples.ko: 아이가 화면을 터치할 때마다 소리가 나요.
examples.en: A sound plays every time the child touches the screen.

explain: 휴대폰이나 주문 기계 화면은 '터치'가 자연스럽고, 버튼은 '누르다'가 더 자연스러워요. '터치 한 번', '터치스크린'처럼 붙어서 자주 나와요. 그림에서는 붓질의 느낌을 말할 때도 터치라고 해요.
explain_en: For phone screens and ordering machines 'touch' sounds natural, while for physical buttons '누르다' (press) fits better. It often appears in set pieces like '터치 한 번' and '터치스크린'. In painting it can also mean the feel of a brushstroke.

examples.en: I walked all day, so my arms and legs hurt.

examples.ko: 우리 아기가 팔다리를 흔들고 활짝 웃어요.
examples.en: The baby waves its arms and legs and laughs happily.
If you swim, your arms and legs get stronger.

examples.ko: 팔다리에 힘이 없어서 계단을 못 올라갔어요.
examples.en: My limbs were weak, so I couldn't climb the stairs.
Mosquitoes bit me, so my arms and legs itch.

examples.ko: 자기 전에 팔다리를 쭉 펴고 스트레칭해요.
examples.en: Before bed I stretch my arms and legs out.

explain: '팔'과 '다리'를 한꺼번에 말할 때 써요. 아플 때는 '팔다리가 쑤시다', '팔다리가 저리다'처럼 말해요. 몸 전체가 아프면 '온몸이 아프다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it when you mean arms and legs together. For aches people say '팔다리가 쑤시다' or '팔다리가 저리다', and for the whole body they say '온몸이 아프다'.
